gaps.sentence: I fell ___ with my best friend over a silly remark.
gaps.explanation: fall out (with somebody) = have an argument and stop being friendly.

gaps.sentence: She was brought ___ by her grandparents.
gaps.explanation: bring up a child = raise, educate them.

gaps.sentence: They set ___ to climb the north face in April.
gaps.explanation: set out (to do) = begin a job/mission with a goal.

gaps.sentence: She always gets round ___ washing up by promising to do it later.
gaps.explanation: get round to = finally find time for; here: avoid a duty — test the preposition after get round.

gaps.sentence: Can I ___ on these boots before buying them?
gaps.explanation: try on = put on clothes/shoes to check the fit.

gaps.sentence: He stole the pens and got away ___ it.
gaps.explanation: get away with something = do wrong without being punished.

gaps.sentence: This job calls ___ someone with patience.
gaps.explanation: call for = require, demand (circumstances call for action).

gaps.sentence: The protesters set ___ at dawn from the village square.
gaps.explanation: set off/out = begin a journey; set up = establish.
